findings.text: the figure path must lie inside ROOT because _receipt_document calls figure.relative_to(ROOT), and the check runs at receipt assembly once the whole twenty-edit sweep has already executed, so an out-of-tree --figure discards the measurement: job 1275975 ran the full sweep and died with ValueError before writing a receipt, while the other four output flags are unconstrained, an asymmetry invisible from the command line. Validating the figure path at parse time in main (:2137) would cost nothing and save an allocation.

the raster figure cannot be redirected: the run subparser (:2137-2144) takes five output paths and --carrier, and run() writes DEFAULT_RASTER_FIGURE at :1855 whenever the terminal state carries a raster flux (the path recorded in the receipt at :1549), so every invocation modifies docs/figures/forward-solve-api/coil-edit-latency/terminal-raster-flux.png inside the tree even when all declared outputs are fenced elsewhere; that file is the reviewed worktree's only dirty entry. Promoting it to a sixth flag, or refusing a default target outside a caller-declared output set, removes a modification no node can fence.

source_revision is git rev-parse HEAD in ROOT evaluated when the receipt is assembled, so it names the commit at assembly time rather than the code that produced the measurement; the reviewed node committed its landing record before measuring and the receipt therefore stamps 9c203931e for a d3849192 code tree, proven only by the module hashes beside the field. Stamping the code identity from the hashes already computed, or recording measurement-time and assembly-time revisions separately, would make the artefact self-describing.

the dispatched done-when requires every output under the reports fence so that nothing under docs/ changes and ends with nothing committed, while the landing contract at line 34 requires the landing record and evidence anchor to go into a commit from the same worktree; for a measurement whose receipt stamps HEAD the two clauses cannot both hold in the intended order, and the natural resolution - commit the record first - is what stamped the wrong source_revision into the receipt, whose stated remedy costs another H200 allocation. The SPEC should state the intended commit order, or the benchmark should stamp code identity rather than HEAD.
